epics.title: Initial Epidemiological Domain Content
epics.jtbd: When a client evaluates a fresh install, I want the system to be populated with real domain content, so that every step of the analytical dossier workflow is demonstrable.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Achieve 100% path coverage for the core epidemiological user journey during acceptance testing
requirements: R1: Create realistic initial domain content (pathogen metadata, isolated strains, analytical dossiers) in the database

R2: Include states for all links: discover protocol through faceted search -> inspect pathogen metadata and isolated strains -> examine researcher analytical dossier -> generate and export signed PDF dossier -> evaluate outbreak transmission root cause -> exercise data subject rights and GDPR compliance

R3: Include states for surveillance authority links: observe real-time surveillance ribbon and KPI status -> monitor active outbreak vectors and transmission distribution -> verify cryptographic integrity of archived protocols -> audit de-identification and privacy compliance
R4: Ensure the content spans all document statuses so every link of the search and evaluation chain is walkable

slices.title: Seed Initial Database Content
slices.jtbd: When implementing the initial content for this epic, I want to insert realistic data, so that the product can be demonstrated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh deployment
When the system initializes
Then the database is seeded with isolated strains and dossier records
And no placeholder 'lorem ipsum' text is used
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 placeholder records present in the initial seed

slices.title: QA Verification for Domain Content
slices.jtbd: When testing the seeded content for this epic, I want to verify all workflows can be traversed, so that the system is ready for client acceptance.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the seeded database
When E2E tests run
Then the full epidemiological search and export flow completes successfully
And the surveillance authority KPI flow works end-to-end
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% pass rate for critical user journey E2E tests

epics.title: Measurement: Epidemiological Analysis Speed
epics.jtbd: When the product is used in production, I want to measure the time it takes an epidemiologist to complete an analysis, so that we can prove the system delivers its core value of speed.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce median time from pathogen search to signed PDF generation by 20%
requirements: R1: Define the goal to enable faster analysis for epidemiologists
R2: Define the question: how much time does an epidemiologist spend from search to final signed PDF dossier?
R3: Implement telemetry to track the end-to-end workflow duration per user session

slices.title: Implement Workflow Duration Telemetry
slices.jtbd: When implementing the metric for this epic, I want to track the start and end times of the analysis flow, so that the core outcome is measured.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the dossier generation workflow
When the user generates a final PDF
Then the telemetry service records the total elapsed time since the search began
And the metric answers the GQM question
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of completed workflows have duration tracked

slices.title: QA Verification for Telemetry
slices.jtbd: When testing the metric for this epic, I want to verify that the telemetry accurately records elapsed time, so that the measurement is reliable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the telemetry pipeline
When an automated test simulates the workflow
Then the metric correctly captures the duration
And integration tests for the metric pass
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero false positives in duration tracking

epics.title: Self-Service Account Recovery
epics.jtbd: When an epidemiologist or authority user is locked out, I want a secure self-service recovery path, so that I can regain access without manual support intervention.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce account lockout support tickets from 100% to 0%
requirements: R1: Implement a self-service recovery path for locked-out user accounts
R2: Ensure the recovery path securely verifies identity before unlocking
R3: Ensure the owner account can also use this recovery path

slices.title: Implement Account Recovery Flow
slices.jtbd: When implementing the recovery flow for this epic, I want to create a secure token-based reset mechanism, so that locked-out users can regain access.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a locked-out user account
When the user initiates recovery
Then a secure, time-bound token is issued
And using it restores access
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% recovery path availability for locked accounts

slices.title: QA Verification for Account Recovery
slices.jtbd: When testing the recovery flow for this epic, I want to verify security and accessibility, so that no unauthorized access occurs.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the recovery flow
When security tests are run
Then expired tokens are rejected
And valid tokens successfully unlock the account
